subject: Aurelia Health — architecture follow-up & reserved capacity test plan
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Jonathan Stone <jonathan.stone@aureliahealth.com>, Emma Park <emma.park@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Aurelia Health — post-call recap & proposed next tests

Hi Jonathan / Emma,

Thanks again for taking time today — quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned.

Call highlights:
- Primary goal: reduce per-request token cost and stabilize inference latency for interactive clinical search at 99th percentile.
- Two evaluation tracks: (A) Redwood Dedicated reserved pool (SLA-backed) and (B) hyperscaler-managed GPU endpoints (preemptible / burst).
- Key unknowns: startup cold-latency with long KV caches, tail latency at 4k sequences, and sustained throughput during concurrent clinician sessions.

Proposed next tests (short):
1) Reserved pool baseline — 2-hour sustained run at target QPS (50 concurrent sessions) with 4k seq distribution. Measure p50/p95/p99 and token cost. Attachment: aurelia-eval-plan-v2.pdf (test matrix + infra steps).
2) Hyperscaler spot / burst baseline — same workload but routed to a widely available hyperscaler config (e.g., A100 preemptible); include repro of cache warm-up pattern.
3) Fallback scenario — simulate capacity loss and confirm Redwood automatic routing to compatible variant model + warm-cache tradeoffs.

Questions for you before we schedule:
- Do you have a preferred hyperscaler region/provider to match prod traffic? (us-west-2 or us-east-1?)
- Any constraints on allowed instance types or egress policy we should be aware of?

Suggested timeline:
- Kickoff + infra prep: Thu or Fri this week
- Dedicated baseline run: next Tue (time TBD)
- Hyperscaler run: next Wed

If that looks good I can loop in our infra ops lead (Rishi) to confirm resource sizing and create the Drive checklist.

Thanks,

--
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192
From: Jonathan Stone <jonathan.stone@aureliahealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emma Park <emma.park@aureliahealth.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Dec 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Aurelia Health — post-call recap & proposed next tests

Stephanie —

Thanks for the clear summary. A couple of clarifications from our side before we schedule:

1) Region: prefer us-east-1 for production parity.
2) Hyperscaler constraints: procurement prefers IAAS spot/low-priority instances (cost optimized) but we need a clear preemption behavior profile — in particular how quickly sessions are re-routed and what client-visible errors look like.
3) SLA expectations: for the reserved path we were hoping to see a 99.9% availability target at p99 <= 250ms for the short inference path; is that in scope for Dedicated?

Also can you share a rough delta on unit cost (per-1000-token) between the reserved profile and hyperscaler spot baseline so we can pre-check finance? A ballpark is fine.

If we can get answers to the above, Emma and I can commit time next week for the runs.

—Jonathan
Jonathan Stone
VP Infrastructure, Aurelia Health
jonathan.stone@aureliahealth.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Jonathan Stone <jonathan.stone@aureliahealth.com>, Emma Park <emma.park@aureliahealth.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 17 Dec 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Aurelia Health — post-call recap & proposed next tests

Hi Jonathan / Emma — answering your points and adding a small technical plan.

Region: us-east-1 is fine; we'll provision reserved capacity there for the baseline.

SLA (Reserved / Dedicated):
- Redwood Dedicated can commit to an operational SLA at the service-level with our reserved pool customers; for this proof we can target an internal acceptance criteria of p99 <= 250ms for the short path under the test workload. Production SLA for enterprise contracts is negotiable (we typically offer SLA tiers tied to committed capacity).

Preemption and fallback behavior (Hyperscaler spot):
- Hyperscaler preemptions manifest as instance termination; Redwood's smart routing will detect capacity loss and automatically fallback to either another region or a smaller model variant depending on the policy you choose.
- For session consistency: we maintain KV cache metadata and route newly arriving requests to the warmed model variant if available; cold-starts will increase latency — we'll quantify this in the fallback test.

Rough cost delta (ballpark):
- Hyperscaler spot baseline: approx $0.06 — $0.12 per 1k tokens depending on instance and region for the configurations we'll test.
- Reserved (Dedicated) profile: approx $0.03 — $0.07 per 1k tokens at our sample committed sizes (reflects amortized GPU + runtime efficiency).
- Note: final numbers depend on model size, token mix, and batch tuning; we'll produce a detailed cost table after the runs.

Proposed technical test matrix (short):
- Test A (Reserved): 4x A100-equivalent reserved nodes, 2-hour steady-state, 50 concurrent sessions, seq dist up to 4k. Output: p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, per-token cost.
- Test B (Hyperscaler spot): matched vCPU/GPU baseline in us-east-1, include preemption injection (terminate 1/3 nodes mid-run). Output: same metrics + failover time and error surface.
- Test C (Fallback warm-cache): pre-populate prefix cache with synthetic sessions, then measure cold vs warmed tail.

Attachments: I uploaded the quick-run CSV template (throughput-bench-20261217.csv) — use it to capture the exact measurement points.

Next steps I propose:
- Stephanie to confirm kickoff time (Thu/Fri) and invite all infra contacts.
- I will provision a reserved pool snapshot and share credentials in the Drive checklist.
- Jonathan / Emma confirm attendees and any IP restrictions for egress.

Thanks — happy to walk through the drive checklist live.

--
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

This looks good. Us-east-1 is correct. We can do the kickoff Fri morning (12/18) for infra prep and then the reserved baseline run on Tue (12/21) as proposed. Emma and I will review the eval plan and upload our internal firewall rules to the Drive checklist.

I'll also ask procurement to expect the high-level cost deltas you sent so we can keep timelines tight.

Confirming attendees: myself, Emma Park (infra lead), and one latency engineer (TBD).

See you Friday.

—Jonathan
